name: Immunodeficiency with Factor I Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Complement Factor I Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of markedly decreased or absent serum complement factor I levels
History of recurrent, severe bacterial infections, especially with encapsulated organisms
Reduced complement hemolytic activity (CH50) with normal or elevated C3 consumption
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the CFI gene
Positive family history of complement deficiency or related immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low or absent serum factor I levels plus either recurrent severe bacterial infections or identification of pathogenic CFI mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other complement deficiencies and immunodeficiencies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Markedly decreased serum complement factor I activity
searchTerms: very low activity of complement factor I

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent invasive infections with encapsulated bacteria
searchTerms: repeated infections with bacteria having capsules

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent low serum C3 levels despite normal C4
searchTerms: persistently low C3 with normal C4 levels
low C3 complement despite normal C4

occasional.symptomName: Chronic fatigue related to recurrent infections
searchTerms: persistent fatigue due to repeated infections
blood infection caused by Neisseria bacteria

laboratory: Markedly decreased serum complement factor I levels
Low serum C3 with normal C4
imaging: Chest X-ray showing recurrent or chronic pneumonia
Brain MRI or CT in cases of meningitis complications
other: Family history of complement deficiency or recurrent infections

distinguishingFeatures: Low C3 and C4 levels in C3 deficiency versus normal C4 in factor I anomaly
Different genetic mutations (C3 gene vs CFI gene)
Normal complement factor I levels in CVID

redFlags: Recurrent severe bacterial infections with encapsulated organisms
Persistent low C3 levels despite normal C4
Family history of complement deficiency or unexplained recurrent infections
references: Józsi M, et al. Complement factor I deficiency: clinical manifestations and molecular basis. Mol Immunol. 2007.
Orphanet: Immunodeficiency with factor I anomaly - ORPHA:200418
Noris M, Remuzzi G. Overview of complement activation and regulation. Semin Nephrol. 2013.
